body_md: `macro_rules!` matches patterns like `($x:expr)` and expands code. `vec![1,2]` is one. Hygienic — names do not leak. Great for DSLs and repetition.
hook: Write code that writes code — declarative macros in 5 lines.

quiz.explain: macro_rules matches syntactic fragments and expands.
quiz.q: How do you define a declarative macro?

takeaway: macro_rules matches patterns and expands code.
trap: Fragment mismatch ($x:expr vs stmt) gives cryptic match error.

body_md: `#[derive(Serialize)]` auto-generates impls via proc macros. Add `serde_derive` to create JSON support instantly. Derive is the most common macro you will use.
hook: One attribute gives you JSON for free.

quiz.explain: Derive macros generate trait impls from AST.

trap: Missing crate feature for derive leaves trait unimplemented.

body_md: Attributes configure items: `#[allow(dead_code)]`, `#[cfg(test)]`, `#[tokio::main]`. Inner `#![allow(...)]` applies to whole file. Docs use `///` sugar for `#[doc]`.
hook: Lines starting with # are not comments — they reprogram the compiler.
takeaway: Attributes drive lints, cfgs, and codegen.
trap: Using #![...] inside fn errors; inner attrs only at module top.

body_md: **Workspaces** share one `Cargo.lock` and `target/` across crates. Root `Cargo.toml` lists `members`. Perfect for app + lib + cli in one repo.
code:
[workspace]
members = ["app", "lib"]
# each member has own Cargo.toml
hook: Monorepo without the pain — workspaces share builds.

quiz.explain: Workspaces unify builds with shared lockfile.
quiz.q: How do you manage app plus lib in one repo?

trap: Version mismatch across members duplicates deps; unify versions.

body_md: **Features** gate optional deps: `serde = { optional = true }`, enable via `dep/feat`. `cargo build --features fast`. `#[cfg(feature="x")]` conditionally compiles code.
hook: Pay only for what you use — features compile optional power.

quiz.explain: Features toggle optional functionality at compile time.
quiz.q: How do you make rayon support optional?

takeaway: Gate optionality with features and cfg.
trap: Feature unification enables a feature unexpectedly; test combos.

body_md: `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]` and `#[cfg(unix)]` compile per-platform. `cfg!` macro checks at runtime. Use for OS-specific syscalls without breaking builds.
hook: Same code, two OSes — cfg picks the right one at compile time.

quiz.explain: cfg selects code per target at compile time.
quiz.q: How do you compile different code per OS?

takeaway: Use cfg for portable conditional compilation.
trap: Forgetting fallback cfg leaves symbol missing on other OS.

body_md: Doc comments `///` render on docs.rs. Include examples — they run as **doctests** via `cargo test`. `# fn main` hides setup. Broken docs fail CI.
hook: Your examples are secretly tests — docs that never rot.

quiz.explain: Code fences in docs compile and run as tests.
quiz.q: What happens to ``` examples in docs?

takeaway: Document with runnable examples as tests.
trap: Doctest using private items fails; expose or hide with text.

body_md: **Criterion** benchmarks with statistics: `c.bench_function("f", |b| b.iter(|| work()))`. Run `cargo bench`. Prevents optimizer from erasing code via `black_box`.
hook: Stop guessing speed — measure with statistics-grade benches.
trap: Benchmarking debug builds measures noise; use --release.

body_md: `cargo doc --open` builds local docs. `# Examples`, `# Panics`, `# Errors` sections are conventions. Intra-doc links `[Vec]` auto-link types.
hook: Great docs follow a hidden template — copy it.
trap: Broken intra-doc links warn; run cargo doc to check.

body_md: Publish with `cargo publish --dry-run` then real publish. Needs unique name, version, license, docs. Use `cargo yank` to block bad versions (never deletes).
code:
$ cargo login
$ cargo publish --dry-run
$ cargo publish
hook: Share your crate with the world in one command.

quiz.explain: publish uploads to crates.io after validation.
quiz.q: How do you release to crates.io?

takeaway: Publish carefully; yank bad versions fast.
trap: Publishing with wildcard deps breaks reproducibility.

body_md: Use `cargo add`, `cargo outdated`, `cargo audit` to manage deps. Pin majors in Cargo.toml (`serde = "1"`). Audit in CI to catch CVEs before prod.
code:
$ cargo add tokio --features full
$ cargo audit
$ cargo update -p serde
hook: Your deps have vulnerabilities right now — find them fast.

quiz.explain: audit checks advisory DB for known CVEs.
quiz.q: How do you check deps for security issues?

trap: Blind cargo update bumps breaking changes; review lock diff.

body_md: Procedural macros take TokenStreams: function-like `my_vec!`, derive, attribute. Built with `syn` + `quote`. Powerful but slow compile — prefer declarative first.
code:
// #[proc_macro_derive(Hello)]
// pub fn hello(input: TokenStream) -> TokenStream { input }
hook: Derive magic runs on real compiler internals — meet proc macros.

quiz.explain: Proc macros transform token streams at compile time.
quiz.q: What do proc macros operate on?

takeaway: Proc macros transform syntax at compile time.
trap: Proc macro panics give span-less errors; use syn spans.
